guide.title: Mozart: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, K. 525 – III. Menuetto (Allegretto)
guide.overview: This is a short minuet, a dance in three beats to the bar, for string quartet. It opens loud and bold in G major. Then it softens and moves to D major. The keys and chords here are estimated by computer. The score came from optical recognition, so small details may be imprecise. The big picture is more reliable: the sections, loud and soft, and the key changes. Who has the tune is only a guess in many bars.

listening_points.headline: A bold opening in G major
listening_points.text: The piece starts loud. The instruments begin together on the same notes in different octaves [m. 0]. Then the first violin probably leads with the main tune [m. 0-3]. The second violin plays the same tune an octave lower, and all move together in block chords.

listening_points.headline: The first part stays loud and rounds off
listening_points.text: The music stays loud throughout [m. 4-8]. The lead is shared and hard to pin down in places. The first part settles back on G major at the end [m. 8]. This whole part is played twice.

listening_points.headline: Suddenly soft: the second part begins
listening_points.text: The volume drops to soft at [m. 9]. The instruments again start together on the same notes. Then the first violin has the tune over a quieter accompaniment [m. 10-12]. The music gets even softer around [m. 13].

listening_points.headline: Loud again, then a quiet turn
listening_points.text: The music jumps back to loud at [m. 14]. The lines become more independent. The chords settle in G major at [m. 15]. Then it goes soft again at [m. 17].

listening_points.headline: A bare solo moment: the cello, then the violin
listening_points.text: The texture thins to single lines. The cello plays alone at [m. 17]. Then the first violin takes over alone at [m. 18]. It sounds like a quiet doorway into a new key.

listening_points.headline: A shift to D major, soft and singing
listening_points.text: The key changes to D major, a new key for this part. The first violin clearly leads a soft tune over a gentle accompaniment [m. 19-24].

listening_points.headline: The soft phrase closes in D major
listening_points.text: The instruments move together in block chords [m. 25-26]. The phrase lands in D major at [m. 26]. It stays soft. This part is repeated.

listening_points.headline: Loud again: the estimated peak
listening_points.text: The last big part starts loud in D major at [m. 27]. The loudest and busiest point is probably at [m. 28]. The first violin probably carries the tune above the rest.

listening_points.headline: Fading down
listening_points.text: The music gets gradually softer [m. 31]. The violins have separate lines. It touches very soft for a moment at [m. 32], then stays soft. A calm D major arrives.

listening_points.headline: A soft singing line in D major
listening_points.text: The first violin clearly leads again, soft over the accompaniment [m. 33-37]. The key stays D major.

listening_points.headline: A closing phrase and a last single line
listening_points.text: The strings play block chords with a sudden accent, then soft [m. 38]. They close in D major at [m. 39]. A last single line from the first violin follows at [m. 40]. It is estimated to be in E minor.

glossary.explanation: A graceful dance in three beats to the bar.
The home note and scale a passage feels built around. Major keys sound brighter, minor keys darker.
Instruments playing the same notes together, in the same or different octaves.
All instruments move together in block chords.
One instrument sings the tune while the others support it.
Loud at first, then at once soft.
